summary: Tom Moor recounts Linear's evolving AI strategy. In early 2023, a small internal team with no AI experience began experimenting with GPT-3-era models, focusing on summarization and similarity. They discovered that most AI features required a solid search foundation, evaluated vector database startups, and pragmatically chose PG Vector on GCP with OpenAI embeddings. Early shipped features included similar issues v1, natural language filters, and Slack-thread-to-issue creation. No copilot was shipped due to quality concerns, and users appreciated the understated approach. By late 2024, a turning point arrived with O3, reasoning models, multimodal APIs, million-token context windows, and DeepSeek, making experiments less brittle. Linear rebuilt search using Turppuffer for hybrid search with Cohere embeddings. Product Intelligence (similar issues v2) launched with query rewriting, hybrid search, reranking, and deterministic rules. Other features include customer feedback analysis, daily/weekly pulses with audio podcast output, and issue-from-video. Two weeks before the talk, Linear launched an agents platform treating agents as first-class users with identity, history, full audit trails, and OAuth installation. Agents work through Linear's mature GraphQL API with granular scopes and new agent-specific webhooks. Demonstrated integrations include Codegen, Bucket, Charlie, and upcoming Intercom Finn integration. A dedicated agent UI surface and SDK are in development, allowing users to see agent observations, tool calls, interrupt agents, and interact more transparently than with human teammates. Tom shares best practices for agent builders: respond quickly with precise acknowledgment, inhabit the platform's language and conventions (e.g., move issues to in-progress), behave naturally in threads, clarify intent before acting by sharing plans, and always add concise value rather than dumping raw LLM output. He envisions agents eliminating the perennial backlog problem, with teams assigning every issue to an agent for a first pass.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Linear treats AI agents as first-class users with identity, history, full audit trails, and OAuth-based installation, managed by team admins with granular scopes.
Agents access Linear through a mature GraphQL API enabling anything a human can do, supplemented by new agent-specific webhooks and mentionable/assignable scopes.
A dedicated agent UI surface and SDK are in development, letting users see agent observations, tool calls, and interrupt agents—more transparent than human teammates.

Best practices for agent builders: respond quickly and precisely, reassure users the request was understood, inhabit the platform's conventions, behave naturally in threads, clarify intent before acting, and add concise value rather than dumping raw LLM output.
Linear's search infrastructure evolved from PG Vector with OpenAI embeddings to Turppuffer hybrid search with Cohere embeddings after backfilling hundreds of millions of rows.
Product Intelligence (similar issues v2) uses a multi-stage pipeline: query rewriting, hybrid search, reranking, and deterministic rules to map relationships between issues.
Late 2024 marked a turning point as reasoning models, multimodal APIs, large context windows, and DeepSeek made experiments substantially less brittle.
Tom envisions agents eliminating the chronic backlog problem—teams can assign every issue to an agent for a first pass, potentially fixing a large percentage automatically.
Early AI features were deliberately understated—no copilot shipped because quality didn't meet Linear's bar; users appreciated seamless, hidden AI value-adds.
Understand Linear's pragmatic approach to AI feature development, prioritizing seamless integration over flashy AI branding

sections.title: Introduction and Linear overview
sections.summary: Tom Moor introduces himself as Head of Engineering at Linear, describing it as a product development tool disguised as an issue tracker, now an operating system for engineering and product teams used by companies like OpenAI, Ramp, and Vercel.

sections.title: Early AI journey (2023)
sections.summary: A 2023 skunkworks team with no AI experience focused on summarization and similarity. After evaluating vector database startups, Linear pragmatically chose PG Vector on GCP with OpenAI embeddings. Shipped features included similar issues v1, natural language filters, and seamless Slack-thread-to-issue creation. No copilot was shipped due to quality concerns; users appreciated the understated approach.

sections.title: Late 2024 turning point and search rebuild
sections.summary: O3, reasoning models, multimodal APIs, large context windows, and DeepSeek marked a turning point. Linear rebuilt search using Turppuffer for hybrid search and Cohere embeddings, completing the backfill in the last two weeks.

sections.title: Product Intelligence and new features
sections.summary: Product Intelligence (similar issues v2) uses query rewriting, hybrid search, reranking, and deterministic rules to produce relationship maps. Other features: customer feedback analysis (claimed to beat 90% of interview candidates), daily/weekly pulse with audio podcast output, and issue-from-video that extracts reproduction steps from bug recordings.

sections.title: Agents platform and demonstrations
sections.summary: Linear launched an agents platform two weeks prior, treating agents as infinitely scalable cloud-based teammates in the same communication space as humans. Demonstrated integrations include Codegen (coding agent producing PRs), Bucket (feature flagging), and Charlie (root-cause analysis from issues with Sentry data).

sections.title: Agent UI vision, architecture, and best practices
sections.summary: Tom describes the future agent UI surface where users can see agent observations, tool calls, and interrupt agents—more transparent than human teammates. Upcoming integrations include Intercom's Finn agent for replying to customers. He envisions agents eliminating the backlog problem. Architecturally, agents are first-class users with identity, history, audit trails, OAuth installation, and admin-managed access. They use Linear's mature GraphQL API with granular scopes and new agent-specific webhooks. A new SDK is in development as an abstraction layer. Best practices for agent builders: respond quickly and precisely, reassure users the request was understood, inhabit the platform's conventions, behave naturally in threads, clarify intent before acting by sharing plans, and add concise value rather than dumping raw LLM output.

demonstrations: Codegen coding agent integrated into Linear—assignable and mentionable, produces plans and PRs, reviewable like any team member's work
Bucket feature-flagging agent—mention to create flags, roll out to percentages of users, check status, all via natural language
Charlie coding agent—mentioned on issues with attached Sentry data, researches recent commits and codebase to determine root cause
Upcoming Intercom Finn integration—mention Finn to reply to customers who reported a fixed bug
limitations: No copilot was shipped because model quality did not meet Linear's quality bar in the early era
Turppuffer hybrid search backfill took a very long time to complete
Audio podcast feature lacks an RSS feed—only available via Linear's mobile or desktop apps
Early similar issues v1 was described as naive simple cosine embedding comparisons
Agent UI surface and SDK are not yet released—expected in a couple of weeks
Building agents on existing API currently requires extra effort; the SDK abstraction layer is still in development
quantitativeClaims: Backfilling hundreds of millions of rows of embeddings took significant time, with the Turppuffer migration completing in the last two weeks
Customer feedback analysis reportedly beat 90% of candidates interviewed for analysis capability
Codegen PR generation took approximately four minutes (shown sped up in demo)
Tom estimates maybe 50% of backlog issues assigned to agents could be fixed by the end of the week
